# untrusted user text, saved verbatim (markdown included); marker hits: 5

Follow-up from testing #1083 on top of the current release. #1083 gets device selection working, but then I ran into two macOS address-space issues. The second one looks like a hard platform limit.

## Environment

- Apple M5 Pro, 48 GB, macOS 26.7 (25G229)
- MoltenVK 1.4.2 (the one bundled with the release)
- Source build: release commit `df5b9b9`, plus the two commits from #1083 cherry-picked (no conflicts), x86_64, `-DKYTY_BUILD_LAUNCHER=OFF`
- Game: GTA V, `PPSA04264` v01.011.001

## 1. `Gen5Driver::Initialize` aborts on macOS (affects every game once #1083 is applied on top of `main`)

Since 165cd884 (`agc: initialize function table in tracked driver memory`), the driver block is mapped at a fixed `DriverDmemBase = 0x0fe0000000`. On macOS x86_64 the guest system-reserved range ends at `HOST_SYSTEM_RESERVED_MAX = 0x0fbfffffff` (`memoryAddressSpace.inc`), so the mapping lands somewhere else and this check fires:

```
--- Fatal Error ---
Error: condition (reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(address) != DriverDmemBase) is true in src/libs/agc.cpp:4176
```

Keeping the 2 MiB block at the top of the macOS reserved range fixes it locally. The game then gets past graphics init:

```diff
+#if defined(__APPLE__) && (defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64))
+// The macOS guest system-reserved range ends at 0x0fbfffffff; keep the driver block inside it.
+static constexpr uint64_t DriverDmemBase = 0x0fbfe00000ull;
+#else
 static constexpr uint64_t DriverDmemBase = 0x0fe0000000ull;
+#endif
```

Nothing else references the address, since `base`/`function_table`/`code_address` are all derived from it. #1083 never hit this because its base predates 165cd884.

## 2. Games with fixed user mappings below `0x7000000000` cannot work on Apple Silicon

With the fix above, GTA V loads `sce_module/libc.prx`, prints `Title ID: PPSA04264` and starts `[RAGE] Main Thread`. It then issues a batch map with `MAP_FIXED` into the PS5 user range:

```
 entries         = 0x903f74ea0
 num_entries     = 1
 flags           = 0x00000010
 [0] start = 0x15b1400000, offset = 0x0000000102200000, length = 0x0000000000010000, prot = 0xf3, type = 0x00, op = 0
--- Guest fault context ---
thread: [RAGE] Main Thread
rax=000000008002000c ... r12=00000015b1400000
--- Error ---
Unhandled host exception: type=1 code=1 pc=0x0000000902bd1ef7 access=2 address=0x0000000000000000
```

`0x8002000c` is ENOMEM. The game then writes through a null pointer. No earlier reserve call mentions that address, so the game picks it itself, assuming the PS5 user range starts at `0x1000000000`. On macOS the guest `USER_AREA` starts at `0x7000000000`.

I checked whether the macOS layout could simply move down to the PS5 one, and it can't:

- **`mmap(MAP_FIXED)` at `0x15b1400000` fails in a plain test program**, both as native arm64 and as x86_64 under Rosetta. The non-fixed hint lands at `0x7000000000` in both cases. So this comes from the macOS VM on Apple Silicon, not from Rosetta.
- **Zerofill segment probes**, using the same linker flags as `kyty_emulator` (`-no_pie -pagezero_size 0x40000 -segaddr ... -image_base 0x700000000000`):
  - The current layout (`SYSTEM_RESERVED` up to `0xFC0000000`, `USER_AREA` at `0x7000000000`) starts fine.
  - Extending `SYSTEM_RESERVED` to `0x1000000000` gets SIGKILL at exec.
  - Any 4 GiB segment at `0x0f00000000`, `0x0fc0000000`, `0x1000000000`, `0x1800000000`, `0x2000000000` … `0x6f00000000` gets SIGKILL at exec.
  - A 4 GiB segment at `0x0c00000000` starts fine.

So `[0xFC0000000, 0x7000000000)` is off-limits to user processes on Apple Silicon. That matches the current `HOST_SYSTEM_RESERVED_MAX`/`HOST_USER_MIN` choice. KytyPS5 runs guest code natively with identity-mapped guest addresses, so any title that maps `MAP_FIXED` between `0x1000000000` and `0x7000000000` (GTA V does at boot) can't run on macOS without guest address translation.

It would probably help to fail with an explicit message in `BatchMap`/`MapDirectMemory` when a fixed request falls in that hole on macOS, instead of returning ENOMEM, and to mention the limitation in the README's macOS section.

_Investigated with the help of Claude Code._
